Let
\[
R=\mathbb F_p[a,b,c]/(a^n,b^n,c^n),
\]
where \(a=T_1-I,\ b=T_2-I,\ c=T_3-I\). Via the regular representation, the function space is \(R\), with the shifts acting by multiplication by \(1+a,1+b,1+c\).

Put
\[
L=a+b+c.
\]
Since \(n\) is a power of \(p\),
\[
c^n=(L-a-b)^n=L^n-a^n-b^n=L^n,
\]
so after the linear change of variables
\[
R\cong \mathbb F_p[a,b,L]/(a^n,b^n,L^n).
\]
Hence
\[
Lf=0
\]
means exactly
\[
f=L^{n-1}g(a,b),\qquad g\in S:=\mathbb F_p[a,b]/(a^n,b^n).
\]
Thus the first equation cuts the dimension down to \(n^2\), before the remaining constraints.

Now write
\[
x=a^q,\qquad y=b^q,\qquad z=c^q.
\]
On \(L^{n-1}S\), we have
\[
z=(L-a-b)^q=L^q-a^q-b^q=-x-y,
\]
because \(L^{n-1}L^q=0\). Also
\[
x+y+z=0.
\]
Therefore, on this subspace,
\[
A=xy+yz+zx=:t,\qquad B=xyz=:r.
\]
So the two remaining operator equations become
\[
(C+tr)g=0,\qquad (t^3+r^2)g=0
\]
inside \(S\), with
\[
z=-x-y.
\]

Compute
\[
t=-(x^2+xy+y^2),\qquad r=-xy(x+y),
\]
and
\[
C=(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)=-(x-y)(x+2y)(2x+y).
\]
Let
\[
P=C+tr,\qquad Q=t^3+r^2.
\]
The ring \(S\) is free of rank \(q^2\) over
\[
E:=\mathbb F_p[x,y]/(x^p,y^p),
\]
with basis \(a^i b^j\), \(0\le i,j<q\). Since \(P,Q\in E\),
\[
\dim_{\mathbb F_p}\operatorname{Ann}_S(P,Q)
=
q^2\dim_{\mathbb F_p}\operatorname{Ann}_E(P,Q).
\]

Because \(E\) is a finite Frobenius algebra,
\[
\dim \operatorname{Ann}_E(P,Q)=\dim E/(P,Q).
\]
It remains to compute this length.

The lowest homogeneous part of \(P\) is
\[
C=-(x-y)(x+2y)(2x+y),
\]
a product of three distinct linear factors since \(p\ge 29\). Thus \(P=0\) has three smooth local branches with tangent lines
\[
x=y,\qquad x=-2y,\qquad 2x=-y.
\]
On each of these tangent lines,
\[
Q=t^3+r^2=-23\,u^6+O(u^7),
\]
for a local parameter \(u\). Since \(p\ge29\), \(-23\ne0\) in \(\mathbb F_p\). Hence \(Q\) cuts each branch with multiplicity \(6\), so
\[
\dim E/(P,Q)=3\cdot 6=18.
\]
Therefore the common kernel of the three operator equations before cyclic symmetry has dimension
\[
18q^2.
\]

Now impose
\[
f(y,z,x)=f(x,y,z).
\]
The cyclic permutation acts on \(S\) by
\[
(a,b)\mapsto (b,-a-b),
\]
an order-\(3\) linear map. Since \(p\ne3\), the fixed-space dimension is
\[
\frac{1}{3}\bigl(\dim W+\operatorname{tr}\tau|_W+\operatorname{tr}\tau^2|_W\bigr),
\]
where \(W=\operatorname{Ann}_S(P,Q)\).

The equations \(P,Q\) are cyclically invariant. Over a field containing a primitive cube root of unity, diagonalize the cyclic action with eigenvalues \(\omega,\omega^2\). The associated graded quotient is a complete intersection cut out by two invariant forms of degrees \(3q\) and \(6q\), so its cyclic character is
\[
\frac{(1-t^{3q})(1-t^{6q})}{(1-\omega t)(1-\omega^2t)}.
\]
Evaluating at \(t=1\) gives trace \(0\). The same holds for \(\tau^2\). Thus
\[
\dim V_n=\frac{18q^2}{3}=6q^2.
\]
Since \(q=n/p\), the final answer is
\[
\boxed{6\left(\frac np\right)^2}.
\]
